themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK compared to a 0.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 2300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting either a sudden influx of unlicensed vendors or a coordinated enforcement/community reporting effort in Sunset Park.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (8-week average)
Timing coincides with warming weather and outdoor vending season onset
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed vendors operating at specific hotspots (parks, transit hubs, schools)? Interview DOH and Street Vendor Project.
Is this a real uptick in vendor activity or increased resident reporting? Survey local block associations.

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK versus a 1.4 weekly average (8-week baseline)—a 191% increase (z-score: 5.42)—indicating possible localized pollution, construction dust, or industrial emissions affecting Sunset Park residents.
evidence: 4 air quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly baseline (8-week average)
191% increase with z-score of 5.42 (high statistical significance)
677 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (456 alterations) suggest ongoing construction activity
reporting_angles: Map the 4 complaints geographically—are they clustered near major construction sites (364 Coney Island Ave or 783 Fourth Ave rezoning projects) or industrial zones?
Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection to cross-reference air monitoring data and identify pollution sources.

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Reports Quadruple
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints surged to 5 TWO WEEKS AGO from a 0.4 weekly average (8-week baseline)—a 1233% spike (z-score: 9.55)—representing the second-highest statistically anomalous issue and signaling potential emerging public safety concerns in specific Sunset Park neighborhoods.
evidence: 5 drug activity complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (8-week average)
1233% increase with z-score of 9.55 (extremely high statistical anomaly)
No corresponding Reddit discussions or recent local news coverage suggests underreported issue
reporting_angles: Obtain NYPD crime data and 311 complaint addresses to pinpoint drug activity hotspots; interview residents and local merchants.
Interview NYPD Narcotics or local precinct commanders about enforcement efforts and what's driving the spike—new supply, turf battles, or seasonal patterns?

themes_detail.label: General 311 Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Broad 311 complaints (general category) jumped to 21 LAST WEEK from a 5.1 weekly average (8-week baseline)—a 310% increase (z-score: 9.83)—suggesting either acute neighborhood-wide infrastructure or service failures or a surge in resident engagement reporting unspecified issues.
evidence: 21 general complaints LAST WEEK vs. 5.1 weekly baseline (8-week average)
310% increase with z-score of 9.83 (highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
Vague category suggests mix of unreported or catch-all issues
reporting_angles: Request detailed 311 complaint text from last week to identify what 'general' issues residents are actually reporting.
Contact 311 or NYC analytics team to understand if spike reflects a specific service failure (e.g., water main break, power outage, missed garbage collection).

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees & Tree Damage
themes_detail.summary: Tree-related complaints (illegal tree damage and overgrown branches combined) spiked 2 WEEKS AGO—8 overgrown complaints (256% above 2.2 baseline, z-score: 5.28) and 9 overgrown complaints (324% above 2.1 baseline, z-score: 4.73)—indicating deferred Parks Department maintenance or environmental stress amid spring growth and recent development activity.
evidence: Illegal tree damage: 8 complaints (2 weeks ago) vs. 2.2 baseline (256% increase, z-score: 5.28)
Overgrown tree/branches: 9 complaints (2 weeks ago) vs. 2.1 baseline (324% increase, z-score: 4.73)
Community board has standing request for 'expand parks and amenities'; 66 new building permits filed suggest active development pressure
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Parks Department about tree inspection schedules, maintenance backlogs, and budget constraints in CD 307.
Map tree complaints geographically to determine if damage clusters near specific development sites (Prospect Farm, 364 Coney Island Ave, 783 Fourth Ave).
